anchorData: FIELD: Mr. Wafula's farm near Kitale, Trans-Nzoia (Rift Valley). Maize variety H614 and common bean variety Rosecoco (GLP-2) planted on the same day (Day 0) in the same field, 3 cm deep, after 25 mm of rain. Maize spacing 75 cm x 25 cm; beans 50 cm x 10 cm. Seeds per row tested: 100 maize and 100 bean seeds each. Mean daily soil temperature about 20 C. TIME-LAPSE EVENTS (typical, rounded): Bean (dicot, epigeal): radicle emerges Day 3; hypocotyl arch pushes through soil and cotyledons lift above ground (emergence) Day 8; cotyledons open and green, first true (unifoliate) leaves Day 12; trifoliate leaves Day 18; branching by Day 25. Maize (monocot, hypogeal): radicle emerges Day 4; coleoptile pierces soil (emergence) Day 7; first leaf unfolds Day 10; 3 leaves Day 17; cotyledon (scutellum) stays underground. GERMINATION COUNTS at Day 14 (out of 100 each): Maize 88 germinated, 12 did not. Beans 80 germinated, 20 did not. Reasons for the 12 non-germinating maize seeds: 5 eaten or rotted by fungi/pests in soil, 4 old stored seed with dead embryos (not viable), 3 planted in a waterlogged low patch (no oxygen). Reasons for the 20 non-germinating bean seeds: 8 hard impermeable seed coat (dormant, healthy-looking), 6 waterlogged low patch (no oxygen), 4 old seed with dead embryos, 2 eaten by pests. Check: 5+4+3=12; 8+6+4+2=20. Dormant-but-viable seeds: 8 beans, 0 maize. After scarifying (nicking) the 8 hard-coated bean seeds and replanting, 7 germinated by Day 7. SEED CLASSES TEST (lesson 4 and 3 style experiment): 20 bean seeds per jar, Day 5 results: water + air + 25 C = 18 germinated; dry = 0; no air (submerged in boiled cooled water with oil layer) = 1; cold (fridge 4 C) = 0. HEIGHT DATA (shoot height in cm, mean of 10 seedlings, measured after emergence): Day: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42. Maize: 3, 12, 30, 62, 98, 125. Bean: 4, 9, 18, 30, 40, 44. Check increases: Maize 9, 18, 32, 36, 27 (slows after Day 35). Bean 5, 9, 12, 10, 4. Maize taller from Day 14 onward. Stem width (mm, mean) Day 14, 28, 42: Maize 6, 14, 22; Bean 2, 4, 6. Root length (cm) Day 14, 28, 42: Maize 10, 25, 40; Bean 8, 18, 26. GROWTH CURVE: both sigmoid; maize steepest (log phase) between Day 21 and 35; bean steepest between Day 14 and 28 then flattening. SECONDARY GROWTH: bean stem base thickens slightly with vascular cambium becoming active; maize (monocot) has no vascular cambium and no true secondary growth; its thickening is from primary growth. Woody example for lesson 5 models: Grevillea robusta (silky oak) or Cypress stem with annual rings. HORMONES: Apical dominance: bean with shoot tip intact: 1 main stem, 0 branches at Day 25; shoot tip (apex) removed at Day 20: 3 lateral branches by Day 32 (auxin from tip inhibits lateral buds; cytokinin promotes them). Seeds soaked in gibberellin solution germinate sooner; abscisic acid maintains dormancy. Auxin on cuttings. CUTTINGS PROJECT (Lesson 8): 30 hibiscus or Duranta stem cuttings per treatment, rooted after 21 days: Plain water 9 rooted; Bulb onion extract 21 rooted; Aloe vera gel 24 rooted; Cinnamon powder 18 rooted. Check percentages: 30%, 70%, 80%, 60%. Aloe best. SELLING (Lesson 10): 60 seedlings of the best treatment sold at KES 20 each = KES 1,200; cost of polythene tubes and soil KES 300; profit KES 900.
characters: Mr. Wafula: farmer in Kitale who planted maize H614 and Rosecoco beans on the same day. Form 3 class at a Kitale secondary school, with teacher Madam Achieng, who films and replicates the field in the lab. Learners: Wanjiru (asks questions on the DQB), Otieno (measures heights), Fatuma (runs the germination jars), Kiprop (leads the cuttings project). Sources: the two time-lapse videos (Bean Time-Lapse 25 days soil cross section; Growing corn time lapse). School tree nursery sells to the community (Kitale) for conservation and income. Dr. Wangari Maathai is the conservation icon (Green Belt Movement) used as inspiration in lessons 8 and 10 only.
outcome: The seeds differ because of differences in seed structure, seed condition and environment, not because of the rain or planting date. Maize (monocot, hypogeal) and beans (dicot, epigeal) have different seed structures and emerge differently; some healthy-looking bean seeds were dormant because of a hard seed coat, while others failed due to pests, being non-viable, or waterlogging (lack of oxygen). Once growing, hormones such as auxin, gibberellins, cytokinins and abscisic acid coordinate growth: primary growth lengthens shoots and roots at meristems, thickening and branching occur differently, and apical dominance explains why beans branch only when the tip is removed.
conventions: Use 'germination' = the radicle emerging from the seed and resumption of embryo growth; 'emergence' = shoot appearing above the soil surface; 'growth' = permanent irreversible increase in size/dry mass; 'development' = changes in complexity and form (differentiation). 'Dormancy' = a viable seed fails to germinate even in favourable conditions. 'Viable' = alive embryo. Monocot: maize, one cotyledon (scutellum), endosperm store, coleoptile and coleorhiza, hypogeal. Dicot: bean, two cotyledons store food, plumule, radicle, testa, micropyle, hilum; epigeal. Units: height cm, width mm, time days, temperature C, money KES. Counts always out of 100 seeds unless stated. Use 'scarification' for breaking the seed coat. Use 'apical meristem' and 'lateral (vascular) cambium'. Hormones named: auxin (IAA), gibberellins, cytokinins, abscisic acid, ethylene. Growth curve = sigmoid with lag, log (exponential), and stationary phases. Always use maize H614 and bean Rosecoco, and the Mr. Wafula farm numbers exactly as in anchorData; do not invent new numbers.
